_meta.name: NutriBite FSSAI & ICMR-NIN Deterministic Health Rulebook
_meta.basis: All per-serving limits apply to one serving as defined on package/plate. 'sugar' means added sugar (g), 'sodium' is mg, 'satFat' is g. Values exceeding 'amber' trigger AMBER; values exceeding 'red' trigger RED. Allergen matches trigger immediate RED.
_meta.disclaimer: Educational and label-decoding guidance based on FSSAI and ICMR-NIN references. Not a substitute for clinical diagnosis or medical advice.

bioBufferRules.description: Actionable 'Eat-It-Anyway' damage-control protocols when a user consumes an Amber or Red food item.

diabetes_spike_buffer.title: Diabetes Spike Buffer
steps: Pre-load 1 tbsp soaked chia or flaxseeds or 4-5 cucumber/salad slices 10-15 minutes before eating to slow gastric emptying.
Take a 12-minute brisk walk starting 15 minutes after the meal to boost insulin-independent glucose uptake.
Avoid pairing with sugary chai, juice, or extra refined carbs in the same sitting.
diabetes_spike_buffer.expectedEffect: Blunts post-prandial glucose peak and flattens the insulin curve.

hypertension_sodium_buffer.title: Hypertension Sodium Buffer
steps: Drink 1 glass of plain tender coconut water (nariyal paani) or have a potassium-rich small banana/guava to help balance the sodium-to-potassium ratio.
Drink plain water steadily across the day and skip added table salt, pickles (achaar), or papad for the next two meals.
Monitor blood pressure later if you are sensitive to sodium fluctuations.
hypertension_sodium_buffer.expectedEffect: Supports potassium-mediated sodium excretion and helps buffer volume/BP pressure.

cholesterol_oil_buffer.title: Cholesterol & Oil Buffer
steps: Start with a glass of warm water with lemon and make your next meal rich in soluble fiber (rolled oats, moong dal, okra/bhindi, or 1 tsp isabgol/psyllium husk).
Keep remaining meals of the day low in saturated fat, palmolein/vanaspati, and deep-fried snacks.
Add a serving of leafy greens or sprouts to increase dietary fiber binding in the gut.
cholesterol_oil_buffer.expectedEffect: Increases soluble fiber binding in the digestive tract and offsets daily saturated/fried fat load.

knownAdditives.name: TBHQ / INS 319
knownAdditives.truth: Synthetic petroleum-derived antioxidant that stops oils going rancid and extends shelf life; allowed by FSSAI in tiny amounts, but best to avoid frequent intake.

knownAdditives.name: INS 627 / INS 631
knownAdditives.truth: Flavour enhancers used with MSG in noodle and chips masalas; they make food hard to stop eating, add hidden sodium, and are best limited if you have gout or high BP.

knownAdditives.name: Sodium Benzoate / INS 211
knownAdditives.truth: Preservative that stops mould in drinks and sauces; permitted at low levels, but it can form benzene with vitamin C and is worth limiting in children.

knownAdditives.name: Liquid Glucose
knownAdditives.truth: Hidden refined sugar syrup that triggers rapid blood glucose spikes.

knownAdditives.name: Maltodextrin
knownAdditives.truth: Starch-based filler that is digested even faster than table sugar, spiking blood glucose, and it often hides in masala and snack seasonings.

knownAdditives.name: Palmolein Oil
knownAdditives.truth: Cheap refined palm oil that is high in saturated fat; common in namkeen, chips and instant noodles, and worse when re-used for frying.

knownAdditives.name: Soy Lecithin / INS 322
knownAdditives.truth: Common emulsifier made from soybeans that keeps chocolate and biscuits smooth; harmless for most people but it is a soy allergen.

knownAdditives.name: Citric Acid / INS 330
knownAdditives.truth: Natural acid from citrus or fermentation used for tang and preservation; safe, though frequent acidic drinks can wear tooth enamel.

knownAdditives.name: MSG / INS 621
knownAdditives.truth: Flavour enhancer that adds a savoury 'umami' punch and hidden sodium; safe for most people in small amounts but best limited with high BP.

knownAdditives.name: Caramel Colour / INS 150d
knownAdditives.truth: Brown colouring made by heating sugar with chemicals; it adds no nutrition and can contain trace by-products, so it is worth limiting in daily colas.

knownAdditives.name: Synthetic Food Colours (INS 102 / 110 / 122 / 129)
knownAdditives.truth: Artificial dyes used to make sweets and drinks look bright; some are linked to hyperactivity in children, so choose naturally coloured foods where possible.

knownAdditives.name: Vanaspati / Hydrogenated Fat
knownAdditives.truth: Solid fat made by hydrogenating oil that can contain trans fat, which raises bad cholesterol and heart risk; FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% of the oil.
